# 2026-06-06 Forecasting Notes

## Market state

- `state.json` was absent again.
- `market.csv`: 378 rows, 95 active, 283 resolved, 0 active questions missing an active prediction.
- New article file: `articles/2026/06/06/articles.jsonl` with 1255 articles.

## New resolutions and lessons

- `441315` resolved to Syria. I had raised Lebanon to 0.90 after Israel-Lebanon/Hezbollah coverage. Lesson: when the wording asks what country Trump says should handle Hezbollah "instead of Israel", direct regional/security-handler framing can beat the country most mentioned in diplomatic implementation.
- `580096` resolved to Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. I had the right person but submitted `Bilawal Bhutto Zardari` without the hyphen. Lesson: exact name formatting matters; preserve article/source spellings for compound names.
- `786553` resolved to Keir Starmer. I overweighted Liz Kendall/Peter Kyle. Lesson: for major UK policy announcements, prime minister announcement risk remains high even when departmental ministers own the file.

## Submitted updates

- `32537`: raised Graham Platner back to 0.72 and moved Mills down after reporting still described him as the all-but-certain Democratic nominee, with no active Mills campaign and strong fundraising despite allegations.
- `596856`: moved Argentina's final warm-up opponent from Iceland to Honduras after June 6 Reuters/ST said Argentina play Honduras later Saturday.
- `183188`: adjusted settlement-funds location toward the concrete Smotrich plan: West Bank 0.32, Jerusalem 0.24, Nablus 0.17, E1 area 0.10, Hebron 0.05.
- `146757`: raised El Obeid to 0.45 after Al Jazeera reported it has been partially encircled for months and hit again around the latest North Kordofan drone attacks.
- `119754`: shifted NBA Game 4 tip-in forecast toward Knicks rebounders after New York took a 2-0 Finals lead and Towns continued strong rebounding/defensive play.
- `523850` and `800177`: modestly updated U.S. scorer markets after Pulisic scored/assisted vs Senegal, Balogun scored the winner, and Antonee Robinson scored vs Germany.
- `235729`: raised Jonathan David and lowered Alphonso Davies/Promise David after Canada coverage emphasized David as the striker/record scorer while Davies and Promise had injury concerns.
- `276967`: replaced Homam Ahmed with Homam Al-Amin and added likely Qatar defensive tacklers from the final squad list.

## World Cup squad-list corrections

- `20324`: removed Xavi Simons from the Netherlands first-goal market because he was not in the final squad list; added Brobbey/Malen/Weghorst.
- `982169`: removed Dejan Kulusevski from Sweden first-goal market because he was omitted with a long-term knee injury; raised Isak/Gyokeres and added Elanga/Nygren/Bergvall.
- `478073`: removed Mostafa Mohamed from Egypt first-goal market because he was left out at Hamza Abdel Karim's expense; raised Salah/Marmoush.
- `482087`: corrected DR Congo from misspelled/not-best options to Bakambu, Wissa, Banza, Mayele, Meshack Elia.
- `144247`: expanded Uzbekistan first-goal market beyond Shomurodov/Fayzullaev to include Igor Sergeev, Masharipov, and Amonov.
- `893085`: removed Jhon Duran from Colombia first-goal market because he was not in the squad; added Luis Suarez, Jhon Cordoba, Juan Camilo Hernandez.
- `56157`: raised Sadio Mane after he scored both Senegal goals in the U.S. friendly and remains the lead attacker.
- `526797`: removed Boulaye Dia from the Senegal two-World-Cups scorer market because he was not in the squad; retained only prior World Cup scorers in the listed squad.
- `230283`: removed Hakim Ziyech from Morocco-Scotland assist market because he was not in Morocco's squad; added Brahim Diaz and midfield creators.
- `200337`: removed Bebe from Cape Verde first-goal market because he was not in the squad list; added Dailon Livramento, Jovane Cabral, and Nuno da Costa.
- `122629`: removed Sebastien Haller from Ivory Coast Canada-authorization market because the current Ivory Coast attacking group is Adingra/Amad/Yan Diomande/Bonny/Wahi/Pepe rather than Haller.

## Left unchanged

- Referee, MT Marivex, Geoffrey Wall, Philippine quake, UFC agreement, Artemis III, Canada bill designation, Japan captain replacement, and the peace-fund question had no decisive new evidence.
- US-Iran framework signer identity remains centered on Abbas Araghchi; June 6 evidence mainly affected deal/no-deal confidence, not the identity of the likely Iranian negotiator.

Baltimore County native Reid Wiseman, who led the Artemis II space crew around the moon in April, appeared virtually in the county council chambers on Monday, recognized as a hero and an inspiration. The council honored Wiseman nearly two months after the crew's 10-day voyage past the moon. The four-person Artemis II crew set the record for the furthest human distance from the Earth. The last human moon landing was Apollo 17 in December 1972. The Artemis II crew was assigned in 2023, with Wiseman named as the commander. He was joined by astronaut Christina Koch, pilot Victor Glover, and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen. "I want to thank you for what you have done for this great nation, and I want to remind you that coming from Baltimore County Public Schools, you are truly an inspiration to the 110,000 students that we have here," Baltimore County Councilman Julian Jones said. "Every kid from this day forward who comes to Baltimore County Public Schools knows that they can reach tremendous heights, such as yourself."
Wiseman grew up in Cockeysville, Maryland, and graduated from Dulaney High School in 1993. He is a long-time Navy veteran and a naval aviator. He was selected to NASA's astronaut program in 2009, which ultimately led to his mission around the moon. "The really important thing for me on this mission was to try to connect with all of humanity on Earth," Wiseman said. "Our mission is Artemis II, but on our patch, we made it look like 'ALL,' Artemis II, because we really wanted to go for all and by all."
Wiseman's father, Bill Wiseman, was in the Baltimore County Council chambers as he was being acknowledged. A local inspiration
